model.description: ROOT DEFECT (architect archaeology 99f2a9d55): Feature was NEVER indexed — this is OMISSION-BY-DEFAULT, not rot. Type-registration was never BOUND to index-creation; the type set lives in MULTIPLE hardcoded PARTIAL sources (templates.ts view-registry = 17 types, no Feature -> no renderMd -> no folder; migrate-to-scenario emitClassSymlinks hardcodes 6; ScenarioIndex has NO byType) and any type in none of them silently gets nothing — so bootstrapSeed corpus-walks Features. Measured NOT a perf issue (boot 1.3s / 5680-unit scan 0.1s). ARCHITECT DESIGN (family, declared-not-defaulted): ONE type-strategy REGISTRY where every ior:class declares exactly one of {typeIndexed | altIndexed(keyField) | singleton} = a SINGLE SOURCE replacing the partial hardcoded lists. Layer 1: DERIVE the view-folders FROM the registry + add ScenarioIndex.byType + a generic template FALLBACK so EVERY declared type renders (the bootstrapSeed corpus-walk is fixed FOR FREE once byType exists — always the symptom). Layer 2 GATE: fails if any type HAS units but NO declaration, or if any typeIndexed type is resolved by corpus scan, with stub-must-fail => omission becomes IMPOSSIBLE, not merely detectable. Keep: read-mostly boot + atomic Feature write. Capture-only, do-NOT-execute — substantial structural req, waits for Tron's scheduling.

acceptanceCriteria.text: ONE type-strategy REGISTRY: every ior:class unit type declares EXACTLY ONE of {typeIndexed | altIndexed(keyField) | singleton} — a SINGLE SOURCE that REPLACES the multiple hardcoded partial lists (templates.ts view-registry, migrate-to-scenario emitClassSymlinks, etc.). Type-registration is BOUND to index-strategy (the missing binding was the root defect).

LAYER 1: the view-folders are DERIVED FROM the registry (not a hardcoded list); ScenarioIndex gains a byType index; a generic template FALLBACK renders any declared type. So EVERY type gets a folder + a renderer by construction — none silently gets nothing. bootstrapSeed's corpus-walk is fixed FOR FREE once byType exists (it was always the symptom, never the disease).

LAYER 2 GATE: FAILS if any ior:class type HAS units but NO registry declaration, OR if any typeIndexed type is resolved by a corpus scan — with STUB-MUST-FAIL (introduce an undeclared type / corpus-scan a typeIndexed type -> RED). Omission becomes IMPOSSIBLE, not merely detectable; the next new type cannot silently get nothing.

Boot is READ-MOSTLY: bootstrapSeed does NOT write per Feature on the boot path — seed-if-absent lazily at point-of-use, or a read-only ASSERT + explicit repair. (Real residual, survives all corrections.)
Feature persistence uses an ATOMIC write (temp+rename): a concurrent boot never tears / lost-updates the Feature file (same class as the token-reembed trap).

AUDIT FINAL (architect-measured 2026-08-17) drives the registry declarations: 7 GENUINE GAPS -> typeIndexed = feature(3), TestCase(1023), modelelement(44), webitem(26), relationship(21), profile(20), gate(7). 4 INTENTIONAL = company/email/phone -> altIndexed (verified scenario/alt/ by-value) + config -> singleton (near-singleton, 2 units). Every type declared, none left in the default-corpus-scan bucket.

supersededACs.text: Boot work is INDEPENDENT of corpus size — O(1) or O(features), NEVER O(all-units). DELETE the bootstrapSeed idx.get-every-unit scan; /api/config must answer without scanning the corpus. Provable: boot get-call-count does NOT grow with total-unit-count.

PREFERRED shape: seed-if-absent LAZILY at point-of-use (the auth path already loads allowedUsers) so boot does ZERO corpus work. ACCEPTABLE alternatives: (a) boot as a read-only ASSERT with an EXPLICIT repair path (no silent mutation at boot); (b) FALLBACK — O(features)-via-type-index + ONE ATOMIC write (temp+rename) + a YIELDING loop. NEVER the synchronous zero-yield O(all-units) loop.

A GATE FAILS if boot touches every unit: instrument the ScenarioIndex.get-call-count AND a boot completion-time BUDGET; STUB-MUST-FAIL — plant a corpus scan at boot and assert the gate goes RED. A boot that re-grows to O(corpus) is caught by construction, not by the next outage.

Close the NON-ATOMIC whole-file read-modify-write on Feature writes: a concurrent boot can tear / lost-update the Feature file (same class as the token-reembed trap). Feature persistence uses an atomic write (temp+rename) so a concurrent reader never sees a torn file and no update is lost.

premiseCorrection.correction1_not-slow: The 'O(all-units) scan makes boot slow / degrades daily / latent outage' mechanism was REFUTED by measurement (expert): boot serves ~1.3s, full 5680-unit scan 0.1s; the 45s 'hang' was a broken TLS probe (node fetch rejects self-signed certs); the 8-min outage was the OLD TypeError crash (fixed). Speed was never the point.

This is a STRUCTURAL regression (a missing type-index), NOT a performance one. RESTORE priority.
premiseCorrection.correction3_archaeology: Architect archaeology (99f2a9d55): the answer to Tron's 'when did you lose that' = NEVER HAD IT. scenario/sprints.md/feature never existed in git; Feature units date to S31 (648136ad6, R31.8). NOT rot -> OMISSION-BY-DEFAULT: type-registration was never BOUND to index-creation. The type set is enumerated in MULTIPLE hardcoded PARTIAL sources and Feature is in none (templates.ts view-registry lists 17 types without Feature -> generator can't renderMd a Feature -> no folder; migrate-to-scenario emitClassSymlinks hardcodes 6; ScenarioIndex has NO byType index). This guarantees the NEXT new type silently gets nothing. AUDIT FINAL (architect-measured, REFUTED the Profile/WebItem-are-alt guess): 7 GENUINE GAPS + 4 intentional (below).
